account: Today there are unusual preparations for an eighteen o'clock gathering in the town hall. Yesterday I saw builder and innkeeper deposit bread in a hall table chest, and lanterns had been placed. Neighbour says the large bread order was paid catering and witnessed innkeeper paying baker; my notes mention an offer of two hundred loaves for 104 emeralds, though I do not have the full terms. Neighbour previously identified builder as coordinating supplies and lighting. Secretary has since confirmed that innkeeper and freight describe the event as an evening community hospitality gathering, with the programme announced at eighteen. Innkeeper invited me, said local helpers are arranging it together, and told me to come as a guest without preparing remarks. He will collect me at my office shortly beforehand. I accepted, and secretary reserved the time. I think the bread and lanterns are for that gathering, but its precise purpose and programme remain unknown to me; I should not assume more than the organisers have said. Several mill-area townsfolk are also repeating a vague report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' One named baker, innkeeper, and neighbour as having been there. I have not seen such a change or learned what that phrase means, so it remains an unexplained rumour, not an established connection to the gathering. Ordinary appointments continue: morning office had no new correspondence, and I am now at the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection, though I have not located the miller. Later I have lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with neighbour at fifteen, and office at sixteen-thirty before the evening escort.
